scope: Test-only regression for the existing Android input/revocation chain: revocation after the input command was dispatched must not claim to retract it and must not replay it. No production source, tool, route, schema, migration or device change.
delivered: FakeAdb gains allow_input/input_entered gates around every `input ...` shell command; defaults are open and the server fixture releases the gate on teardown, so all existing Android tests keep their prior behavior.

New regression: submit and approve an append_ascii input, hold the fake device after the input command enters the worker, revoke the grant, then release. The actual text changes to `hello world` and the run succeeds with action effect applied (revocation cannot retract an already dispatched input); fake.writes is exactly 1, so there is no replay.
After revocation the old observation cannot authorize another input: request_for fails, and fake.writes stays 1.
No assertion was weakened, no production timeout/budget was shortened, and no real device/account/model was used.

android_integration_and_model.notes: 19 integration + 20 model nodes on the final formatted source; real V2 SQLite, managed Python worker, isolated fake ADB; no actual device.

validation.ruff: both changed test files pass ruff check and format check (no reformat needed)

retained_first_failures.reason: A PowerShell in-place replacement once inserted a literal CRLF escape into the test source; the syntax error was fixed before any final run. No production code was touched.

The first version asserted run state succeeded-or-failed and effect applied-or-unknown. The actual isolated fake-device behavior is succeeded/applied (revocation does not retract a dispatched input), so the assertion was tightened to lock that contract.
